deck.audience: venture capital investors and startup founders evaluating generative AI opportunities

brief.title: Generative AI's Act Two: From Technology Hammer to Real Value
brief.one_liner: Sequoia Capital's analysis of how generative AI is transitioning from novelty demos to end-to-end solutions that solve real human problems, with data on retention, revenue, and market structure.
brief.goal: Understand the shift from Act 1 (technology-out) to Act 2 (customer-back) in generative AI, recognize the retention challenges facing AI-first apps versus incumbents, and identify the characteristics of companies likely to win in the next phase.

slides.title: Generative AI's Act Two: From Technology Hammer to Real Value
slides.objective: Cover slide with the deck title, Sequoia Capital attribution, and publication date (September 2023). Set the stage with a compelling visual framing.

slides.title: Six Decades of Technological Progress Converged to Enable Generative AI
slides.objective: Present the three foundational technology waves — Moore's Law (6 decades of compute), the internet (4 decades of training data), and mobile/cloud (2 decades of distribution) — as a timeline or layered visual showing how they accumulated to create the conditions for generative AI.

slides.title: GenAI Startups Surpassed $1B Revenue Faster Than SaaS Ever Did
slides.objective: Highlight the rapid commercial traction of generative AI startups, noting >$1B in startup revenue in months versus years for SaaS. Reference standout examples: ChatGPT (fastest-growing app), Midjourney (hundreds of millions in revenue with 11 employees), and Character.ai (2-hour average session time).

slides.title: AI-First Apps Show 14% Median Retention vs. 51% for Incumbents
slides.objective: Present a comparative bar chart or side-by-side visualization using the mobile app retention data. Incumbents (WhatsApp 85%, Instagram 64%, YouTube 64%, TikTok 60%, Snapchat 51%, Roblox 41%, Tinder 34%, Candy Crush 32%, Duolingo 30%) vs. AI-First Companies (Character.ai 41%, Runway 27%, Remini 14%, ChatGPT 14%, Lensa 12%). Emphasize the stark median gap: 51% vs. 14%.

slides.title: YouTube Leads Incumbents at 85% Monthly Active Usage
slides.objective: Show the second incumbent benchmark chart with monthly usage rates: YouTube 85%, Instagram 73%, TikTok 69%, Snapchat 67%, WhatsApp 63%, Roblox 61%, Tinder 54%, Duolingo 50%, Candy Crush 48%, with a 63% median. This contextualizes the high bar AI apps must clear.

slides.title: Act 1 Was Technology-Out; Act 2 Is Customer-Back
slides.objective: Create a two-column comparison contrasting Act 1 (foundation models as the entire solution, novelty demos, lightweight wrappers, poor retention) versus Act 2 (foundation models as a piece of a comprehensive solution, new editing interfaces, multi-modal workflows, end-to-end problem solving). Reference Harvey, Glean, Character, and Ava as Act 2 exemplars.

slides.title: Market Map Reorganized by Use Case, Not Model Modality
slides.objective: Present the conceptual shift in how the Sequoia generative AI market map is now organized — from model modality (text, image, code) to use case, reflecting the evolution from technology hammer to actual value delivery. Emphasize the increasingly multi-modal nature of applications, referencing Act 2 exemplars like Harvey (legal), Glean (enterprise search), Character and Ava (companionship) as illustrations of use-case-driven categories. Note that this reorganization mirrors the broader Act 1 to Act 2 transition.

slides.title: Key Takeaways: What Separates Winners in Act Two
slides.objective: Summarize 4-5 actionable implications: (1) Retention is the critical challenge — AI-first apps at 14% median vs. 51% for incumbents; (2) Foundation models should be a component, not the whole product; (3) Multi-modal, workflow-integrated solutions will win; (4) The $1B+ revenue milestone proves real demand exists despite hype cycles; (5) Companies solving end-to-end human problems will define Act 2.
